title: Online safety and media literacy
outcome: Online safety & media literacy (Safer Internet Day).
source_note: Owner brief supplies date, period and verbatim outcome from LAUNCH Weekly Spring row150. Source workbook not reopened. Accepted LAUNCH format supplies structure/style only. Official education, privacy, cyber-security and media-literacy guidance checked for this narrow lesson; no claim of complete statutory curriculum coverage. Original fictional examples and offline tasks.

definitions.privacy: Control over who can access personal details. Settings can limit an audience, but cannot stop every copy or later share.
definitions.digital_footprint: Information about a person that exists online, from their own actions and what others share or collect. Some information can last or be copied.
definitions.media_literacy: Skills for asking questions about what a message claims, where it came from and what supports it.
definitions.manipulated: Changed or edited. An edit can alter meaning. Some edits are harmless, so context matters.
definitions.misleading: Likely to give a wrong impression. A real image or true detail can mislead when context is missing.

key_points: Check the audience, location sharing and who can contact or tag a person. Ask trusted staff for help with unfamiliar settings.
Settings reduce some risks. A private post can still be copied or shared. Other people and services can add to a footprint.
A polished image, many likes or repeated claims do not prove truth. Pause and check source, date, full context and other evidence.
When something goes wrong, stop engaging, seek trusted adult help and use safe reporting tools with support. Being targeted by an unwanted message is not the learner’s fault.

scene.title: A post about an activity
scene.text: An invented learner sees a post saying the next activity is cancelled. It shows a cropped notice with no date. A second post shows an edited picture of the empty activity room. The learner pauses before sharing and asks trusted school staff to check the full notice.
scene.model: The crop leaves out the date and the edited room picture cannot prove a cancellation. The learner can wait and ask staff for the current full notice. Many shares would not make either post reliable.
discussion: What detail or evidence is missing?
What safe action could the learner take before sharing?

examples.title: A cropped notice
examples.shown: The crop shows only the words Activity cancelled. No date or sender is shown.
examples.context: Full invented notice dated 14 January 2027: Activity cancelled on 14 January 2027. The next activity on 21 January 2027 will run as usual.
examples.answer: Misleading context. The words are real within the invented notice, but the crop hides the old date and next-session line. Check the current full notice with staff.

examples.title: An edited room picture
examples.post: EMPTY ROOM PROVES THE ACTIVITY IS OFF
examples.shown: A simple drawing has had the activity materials removed. The post gives no current notice.
examples.context: The original invented drawing shows materials in the room. A changed picture cannot establish the current plan.
examples.answer: Manipulated image used as weak evidence. Editing can change a scene. Ask for the current full notice; do not rely on the image or likes.

examples.title: A checkable update
examples.post: The next activity is on. Check the current notice with staff.
examples.shown: The message is dated 21 January 2027 and points to the full notice available from staff.
examples.context: Full invented notice dated 21 January 2027: The activity on 21 January 2027 is on as planned. Ask trusted school staff if you need the first step explained.
examples.answer: Better supported within this invented exercise because a current full notice can be checked. A date or neat design alone is not proof; actual verification matters.

privacy_sort: Use the intended limited audience and check it before posting.
Keep location sharing off unless a safe need is agreed with a trusted adult.
Who can message or add a tag
Limit unfamiliar contact and review tags with trusted help.
Ask consent and leave private details out. A no must be respected.
response_steps: Pause. Stop replying or sharing. Move away from the content if needed.
Tell a trusted adult or school staff privately. Ask them to help decide the safe next step.
Use report, block or mute tools with adult support where suitable. Tell staff if the first route does not help.
Do not forward, download or copy harmful or private content to prove it. Let trusted staff guide any safe record through school procedure.

checklist.title: My online safety checklist
checklist.instruction: Keep this card privately. Tick a step to remember or leave it blank. Use the invented learner instead or pass. This is a reminder, not a check of your accounts.
items: I pause before I post or share.
I check who could see it and leave private details out.
I ask before I share another person’s information or image.
I can ask a trusted adult to help check privacy, location and contact settings.
I check the source, date, full context and evidence before I trust a claim.
If something goes wrong, I stop engaging and ask trusted school staff for help.
fields: One step I want to remember: ____________________
A support type that could help: ____________________
checklist.privacy: No names, usernames, passwords, account details, screenshots, private incidents or device checks. Keep the card with you. It is not collected, photographed, displayed or compared.

self_assessment.title: Learning self check
items: I can explain one limit of privacy settings.
I can give a reason to check a misleading post.
I can suggest a safe next step and a support type.
self_assessment.note: Tick learning only. All boxes start blank. Pass or use a fictional example. This is not a judgement of someone’s online history or safety.

help_route: Support may come from a trusted adult, school staff, a family doctor or a suitable helpline. Ask trusted school staff privately to help find an age-appropriate route and use reporting tools safely. If the first adult is unavailable or unhelpful, try another trusted adult through the agreed route. For immediate concern, get school staff straight away and use the school urgent procedure. No named service, number, website or live online task is needed.
step_out: Before the lesson, quietly agree the familiar pause signal and supervised place/route with the learner. A pupil may show a pause card or use the usual aid without a public explanation. A staff member acknowledges and supports the agreed route; never send a learner off alone or remove supervision. Offer a neutral task and a supported return, or arrange a later private catch-up. Pass/step-out is not failure and does not require personal disclosure.
safeguarding: Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Keep actual concerns and identifying details out of class tasks and shared learning evidence; use the school separate safeguarding record. If a learner cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press. The personal checklist stays with the pupil; scribe only by agreement and return it.
practice_rule: All class questions, optional pair talk and worked examples use invented third-person scenes. No one has to show a phone, account, message, search history, personal checklist or real incident. Use print cards offline, including for cover. Private personal reflection can be replaced by a fictional card, blank or pass. Usual aids, typing and exact scribe/readback remain available.

routes.Supported: Use two clear choices, word bank, starter and visible fictional model. Point, draw, say or type; exact scribe and readback available. Identify a privacy limit, one missing clue and one safe help step.
routes.Independent: Use the glossary, full invented source cards and normal aids. Explain a privacy choice and its limit, compare each post with its source and suggest a safe response with support.
routes.Aspire: Keep usual aids. Explain how a crop or edit changes meaning, weigh evidence rather than appearance, and adapt the safe response if the first adult or reporting route is unavailable. Extra personal detail is never required.

tiered_packs.rule: Choose one separate tier pack per pupil. All cover the same outcome; scaffolds differ. Shared source cards and private checklist in Support Cards. No live account or online access required.

success: Explain a privacy choice and why settings have limits.
Use source/context evidence to question an invented post.
Choose a safe response and support type if something goes wrong.
timing: Quiet set-up; preview invented offline cards and agreed supervised pause route.
Private fictional claim: many likes prove a post true.
Model privacy controls, digital footprint and copied-post limit.
Compare a crop with the full notice; private hinge and recheck;15–16 reset included.
16–22 chosen tier checks three invented posts;22–27 safe-response rehearsal and private checklist;27–28 reset included.
Fictional privacy limit, evidence reason and safe-help response plus learning check;33–34 reset included.
One next step and own response in usual mode.
Private fictional exit and generic help reminder.

scaffolds.start: Many likes do not prove ___ because ___.
scaffolds.model: Many shares do not prove the activity is cancelled.
A setting can limit who sees a post, but a viewer may copy it.
They could ask staff to check the full current notice.

scaffolds.start: The post claims ___. It leaves out ___.
scaffolds.model: The crop claims the activity is off today. It leaves out the old date.

scaffolds.start: The learner could stop ___ and ask ___.
scaffolds.model: They could stop replying and ask trusted school staff for help.

scaffolds.start: I can explain ___ using the invented ___.
scaffolds.model: I can explain the missing context using the invented notice.

scaffolds.start: A safer next step in the story is ___.
scaffolds.model: A safer next step is asking staff before sharing the post.

hinge.question: A popular post uses a cropped notice with no date. What should the learner do?
hinge.A: Share it now because many people liked it.
hinge.B: Pause and check the full current notice with trusted staff.
hinge.decision: Check privately through words, pointing, typing or usual aid. If B or safe equivalent with a reason, proceed. For A, unclear or no response, re-model missing context and use parallel check. Pass is not a wrong answer.

parallel.question: A post uses an edited picture of an empty room. Does that prove the next activity is off?
parallel.A: No. Check the current full notice with trusted staff.
parallel.B: Yes. A clear picture always proves the claim.

misconceptions: A private setting stops all copies and removes every trace.
It can limit an audience. Copies, collection or other people’s posts may still exist; ask for help.
A polished picture or lots of likes proves a claim.
A real picture may lack context or an edit may alter it. Check the source and evidence before sharing.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Short plain definitions, full fictional source beside each claim, visible model, seven scaffold banks and fewer written responses.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Choice, processing time, familiar aid, typing, pointing, drawing or exact scribe/readback. Optional fictional pair talk; no public questioning.
adaptations.SEMH: Predictable mild third-person examples, no personal online incident questions, private checklist, blank/pass and supervised step-out with supported return.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Accessible print and seating, usual communication tools and quiet resets; all tasks possible offline without a phone.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Explain crop, source, footprint and privacy with short fictional examples. Usual language support conveys the learner’s own meaning.

cold_call_label: Optional private fictional check bank; no public personal questions.

cold_call.F: Who could the invented learner tell privately?
cold_call.M: Which missing detail changes the crop’s meaning?
cold_call.H: Why is the checkable full notice stronger evidence than likes or an edited image?

ta_focus.I_do: Model audience and copy limit using the invented post only.
ta_focus.We_do: Offer frame and source comparison. Check privately; do not ask about actual accounts or incidents.
ta_focus.Independent: Observe fictional reasoning and safe help step. Record access/content prompts honestly. Supervise pause route and pass any disclosure to safeguarding lead.

evidence: Record learning from fictional tasks: privacy choice and limit; missing context/edit and evidence reason; safe next step and support type; chosen tier, usual aids, actual prompts, one NS and own response. Do not collect the personal checklist or real incident/account data. No claim of real-world account safety follows from classroom performance.
where_this_leads: This helps me question information, respect privacy and ask for support in learning, relationships and future work.

paragraphs: Online safety learning guide
Online safety & media literacy (Safer Internet Day).
Use the invented learner for class work. You can write, type, point, draw or use your usual aid. A scribe can record your exact words and read them back. No personal account or story is needed.
The invented learner

paragraphs: Teacher and cover planner
Online safety and media literacy
Thursday 21 January 2027 · P4 · 40 minutes · Year A
LAUNCH · pair aged 14–16 · Spring 1 Week 3 · formative
Theme Resilience & Change. Thread tags: SMSC S/So; British Values IL/MR.
Exact outcome
Online safety & media literacy (Safer Internet Day).
Purpose and success
Explain a privacy choice and why settings have limits.
Use source/context evidence to question an invented post.
Choose a safe response and support type if something goes wrong.
Non specialist preparation

Read Staff Answers. Print one tier pack per learner, Support Cards and glossary; keep the staff learning record separate. Prepare books or usual aids. All examples are invented and offline. No live account, device, login or online search is needed. Quietly agree the pause signal, supervised route and staff response.
Forty minute sequence
The three one-minute resets at 15–16, 27–28 and 33–34 are included in forty minutes. Pair talk is optional and uses fictional examples only.
Teaching and response routes
Arrival and starter

0–4: calm set-up, preview the sequence and privately agree the supervised pause route. 4–6: present the fictional claim that many likes prove a post true. Invite a private choice and reason. Explain that popularity cannot establish truth. Privacy controls can help but cannot stop every copy or share.
Model and guided check

6–11: teach privacy settings and digital footprint using the invented profile choices. Compare the small audience and location-off options. 11–15: show an invented post, teach source, date and full context checks, then use the main hinge. Re-model and use the parallel if needed. 15–16: quiet reset.
Practice and learning

16–22: use the invented examples to identify a changed or misleading element and a check. 22–27: make a safe response plan for the third-person online mix-up. 27–28 reset. 28–33: record fictional learning, offer a private checklist and learning self-check. 33–34 reset. 34–38: one next step and learner response. 38–40: private exit and help route.
Supported

Use two clear choices, word bank, starter and visible fictional model. Point, draw, say or type; exact scribe and readback available. Identify a privacy limit, one missing clue and one safe help step.
Independent
Use the glossary, full invented source cards and normal aids. Explain a privacy choice and its limit, compare each post with its source and suggest a safe response with support.
Aspire

Keep usual aids. Explain how a crop or edit changes meaning, weigh evidence rather than appearance, and adapt the safe response if the first adult or reporting route is unavailable. Extra personal detail is never required.
Model and fade

The crop leaves out the date and the edited room picture cannot prove a cancellation. The learner can wait and ask staff for the current full notice. Many shares would not make either post reliable. Show the model first, then leave the next choice and reason to the learner. Keep glossary, frames and usual aids. Do not collect private checklist choices.
TA focus

Reinforce that a polished post or high share count does not prove a claim. Offer read-aloud, pointing, exact scribe and readback as normal access. Observe fictional explanations and record actual content prompts separately. Acknowledge the pause signal, keep supervision and route any disclosure to the safeguarding lead.
Aids for each task
Each task keeps a word bank, sentence starter and visible model. Choose one tier per learner. All tiers retain privacy, media checks, a safe response and a private checklist.
Starter claim
Words: likes, claim, proof, check
Start: Many likes do not prove ___ because ___.
Model: Many shares do not prove the activity is cancelled.
Privacy model
Words: audience, location, contact, copy
Start: A setting can limit ___ but ___.
Model: A setting can limit who sees a post, but a viewer may copy it.
Private hinge
Words: crop, date, context, source
Start: Before sharing, the learner could ___.
Model: They could ask staff to check the full current notice.
Post check
Words: claim, source, date, edit, evidence
Start: The post claims ___. It leaves out ___.
Model: The crop claims the activity is off today. It leaves out the old date.
Safe response
Words: pause, stop, tell, report, support
Start: The learner could stop ___ and ask ___.
Model: They could stop replying and ask trusted school staff for help.
Learning self check
Words: explain, reason, prompt, help
Start: I can explain ___ using the invented ___.
Model: I can explain the missing context using the invented notice.
Feedback and exit
Words: next step, response, private, adult
Start: A safer next step in the story is ___.
Model: A safer next step is asking staff before sharing the post.
Prompt ladder

Point to the place or instruction. Ask a short private question. Rephrase. Offer a scaffold or choice. Model the first step only, then return the task. Allow processing time and retain the usual aids. Record content prompts honestly.
Checks and planned access
Main hinge

A popular post uses a cropped notice with no date. What should the learner do? A: Share it now because many people liked it. B: Pause and check the full current notice with trusted staff. Correct B. Check privately through words, pointing, typing or usual aid. If B or safe equivalent with a reason, proceed. For A, unclear or no response, re-model missing context and use parallel check. Pass is not a wrong answer.
Parallel hinge

A post uses an edited picture of an empty room. Does that prove the next activity is off? A: No. Check the current full notice with trusted staff. B: Yes. A clear picture always proves the claim. Correct A.
Cognition and Learning
Short plain definitions, full fictional source beside each claim, visible model, seven scaffold banks and fewer written responses.
Communication and Interaction
Choice, processing time, familiar aid, typing, pointing, drawing or exact scribe/readback. Optional fictional pair talk; no public questioning.
SEMH
Predictable mild third-person examples, no personal online incident questions, private checklist, blank/pass and supervised step-out with supported return.
Sensory and Physical
Accessible print and seating, usual communication tools and quiet resets; all tasks possible offline without a phone.
EAL
Plan in any language. Explain crop, source, footprint and privacy with short fictional examples. Usual language support conveys the learner’s own meaning.
Optional private story checks
F: Which setting could limit who sees a post?
M: What is missing from the cropped post?
H: Why might two matching reposts still fail to confirm a claim?
Misconceptions
A private setting stops all copies and removes every trace. It can limit an audience. Copies, collection or other people’s posts may still exist; ask for help.
A polished picture or lots of likes proves a claim. A real picture may lack context or an edit may alter it. Check the source and evidence before sharing.
Privacy and safe support
Personal checklist

No names, usernames, passwords, account details, screenshots, private incidents or device checks. Keep the card with you. It is not collected, photographed, displayed or compared. Use only actions or symbols. No account names, passwords, locations, personal incidents or evidence copies. A fictional checklist, blank or pass is valid.
Discreet supervised step out

Before the lesson, quietly agree the familiar pause signal and supervised place/route with the learner. A pupil may show a pause card or use the usual aid without a public explanation. A staff member acknowledges and supports the agreed route; never send a learner off alone or remove supervision. Offer a neutral task and a supported return, or arrange a later private catch-up. Pass/step-out is not failure and does not require personal disclosure.
Help by type

Support may come from a trusted adult, school staff, a family doctor or a suitable helpline. Ask trusted school staff privately to help find an age-appropriate route and use reporting tools safely. If the first adult is unavailable or unhelpful, try another trusted adult through the agreed route. For immediate concern, get school staff straight away and use the school urgent procedure. No named service, number, website or live online task is needed.
Safeguarding

Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures where needed. Keep actual concerns and identifying details out of class tasks and shared learning evidence; use the school separate safeguarding record. If a learner cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press. The personal checklist stays with the pupil; scribe only by agreement and return it.
Learning evidence

Record learning from fictional tasks: privacy choice and limit; missing context/edit and evidence reason; safe next step and support type; chosen tier, usual aids, actual prompts, one NS and own response. Do not collect the personal checklist or real incident/account data. No claim of real-world account safety follows from classroom performance.
Feedback and marking

VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step in green; // self-edit; ? read this back to me; E actual evidence banked; R responded. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping.
Book first and cover fallback

Use books or usual modes for fictional explanations. If display equipment fails, read the printed invented examples from Support Cards. Keep the same forty-minute sequence and private response modes. Never substitute live feeds or pupil experiences. Staff do not request, copy or circulate private or harmful content as lesson evidence.

paragraphs: Staff answers and cover notes
Suggested responses for the invented offline cases. Accept other safe, reasoned answers. Never assess a learner’s personal online life.
Privacy
Control over who can access personal details. Settings can limit an audience, but cannot stop every copy or later share.
Digital footprint
Information about a person that exists online, from their own actions and what others share or collect. Some information can last or be copied.
Media literacy
Skills for asking questions about what a message claims, where it came from and what supports it.
Manipulated
Changed or edited. An edit can alter meaning. Some edits are harmless, so context matters.
Misleading
Likely to give a wrong impression. A real image or true detail can mislead when context is missing.
Invented scene key
The crop leaves out the date and the edited room picture cannot prove a cancellation. The learner can wait and ask staff for the current full notice. Many shares would not make either post reliable.
Privacy choices

A smaller audience, location off and checking who can tag or contact the learner may reduce exposure. Settings differ between services and can change. They cannot guarantee that a recipient will not copy, capture or pass on content. A digital footprint can include a person’s posts and information other people share about them.
Supported

Use two clear choices, word bank, starter and visible fictional model. Point, draw, say or type; exact scribe and readback available. Identify a privacy limit, one missing clue and one safe help step.
Independent
Use the glossary, full invented source cards and normal aids. Explain a privacy choice and its limit, compare each post with its source and suggest a safe response with support.
Aspire

Keep usual aids. Explain how a crop or edit changes meaning, weigh evidence rather than appearance, and adapt the safe response if the first adult or reporting route is unavailable. Extra personal detail is never required.
Examples and check answers
A cropped notice

ACTIVITY CANCELLED TODAY The crop shows only the words Activity cancelled. No date or sender is shown. Full source: Full invented notice dated 14 January 2027: Activity cancelled on 14 January 2027. The next activity on 21 January 2027 will run as usual.
Suggested answer
Misleading context. The words are real within the invented notice, but the crop hides the old date and next-session line. Check the current full notice with staff.
An edited room picture

EMPTY ROOM PROVES THE ACTIVITY IS OFF A simple drawing has had the activity materials removed. The post gives no current notice. Full source: The original invented drawing shows materials in the room. A changed picture cannot establish the current plan.
Suggested answer
Manipulated image used as weak evidence. Editing can change a scene. Ask for the current full notice; do not rely on the image or likes.
A checkable update

The next activity is on. Check the current notice with staff. The message is dated 21 January 2027 and points to the full notice available from staff. Full source: Full invented notice dated 21 January 2027: The activity on 21 January 2027 is on as planned. Ask trusted school staff if you need the first step explained.
Suggested answer
Better supported within this invented exercise because a current full notice can be checked. A date or neat design alone is not proof; actual verification matters.
Main hinge

A popular post uses a cropped notice with no date. What should the learner do? Correct B: Pause and check the full current notice with trusted staff. Check privately through words, pointing, typing or usual aid. If B or safe equivalent with a reason, proceed. For A, unclear or no response, re-model missing context and use parallel check. Pass is not a wrong answer.
Parallel hinge
A post uses an edited picture of an empty room. Does that prove the next activity is off? Correct A: No. Check the current full notice with trusted staff.
What a check can establish

Compare the full original item, its source and date and an independent reliable source where possible, with trusted staff support. Reposts that copy the same claim are not independent checks. Appearance, likes or a missing clue alone do not prove truth or falsity. It is valid to pause and say there is not enough evidence.
Safe delivery and evidence
If something goes wrong

Support may come from a trusted adult, school staff, a family doctor or a suitable helpline. Ask trusted school staff privately to help find an age-appropriate route and use reporting tools safely. If the first adult is unavailable or unhelpful, try another trusted adult through the agreed route. For immediate concern, get school staff straight away and use the school urgent procedure. No named service, number, website or live online task is needed.

A staff member acknowledges and supports the agreed route; never send a learner off alone or remove supervision. Offer a neutral task and a supported return, or arrange a later private catch-up. Pass/step-out is not failure and does not require personal disclosure.

Keep actual concerns and identifying details out of class tasks and shared learning evidence; use the school separate safeguarding record. If a learner cannot identify a trusted adult, support them privately and do not press. The personal checklist stays with the pupil; scribe only by agreement and return it.
Evidence and marking

Do not collect the personal checklist or real incident/account data. No claim of real-world account safety follows from classroom performance. R only when Voice and Audience are present, one NS is set and the pupil responds in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio; staff confirm any mapping.
Self assessment

Ready to explain, With a prompt and Need another example describe learning only. All choices start blank. The personal checklist is a private planning aid and cannot certify that a learner is safe online. Do not collect it or infer current online risk from a blank or a choice.
Source and scope

Current statutory RSE and health guidance in force from September 2026 informs the narrow online and media content. Supplementary official education, privacy, cyber-security and information-evaluation guidance was checked. Owner brief supplies date, period and verbatim outcome from LAUNCH Weekly Spring row150. Source workbook not reopened. Accepted LAUNCH format supplies structure/style only. A learner plans to share a photo of a model they made. They do not need to show their face, school badge or location. They can choose a smaller audience, keep location off and check tag and contact controls with trusted adult support. They ask before sharing anyone else’s work or image.

paragraphs: Words for online safety
Use these words with the invented examples. Plan in any language or ask for words to be read.
A sentence frame
This choice could help because ___. It cannot stop ___. The post needs a check because ___. The learner could ask ___ for help.
Help and privacy
Keep the personal checklist private. No real account, passwords or incidents. Use the agreed pause signal or ask trusted school staff privately.
table_cells: Control over who can access personal details. Settings can limit an audience, but cannot stop every copy or later share.
Information about a person that exists online, from their own actions and what others share or collect. Some information can last or be copied.
Skills for asking questions about what a message claims, where it came from and what supports it.
Changed or edited. An edit can alter meaning. Some edits are harmless, so context matters.
Likely to give a wrong impression. A real image or true detail can mislead when context is missing.

Exact outcome
Online safety & media literacy (Safer Internet Day).
Learning and evidence

Explain privacy settings and digital footprint. Check original invented posts for source, date, changed image or missing context. Plan a safe response and a generic support route. Offer the private personal online-safety checklist. Record fictional learning, usual aids, actual prompts, one NS and learner response. Do not collect personal checklist details or account information.
Forty minutes
Access and care

Three separate tier packs, glossary, visible models, pointing, typed route, exact scribe and readback. Pair talk optional and fictional. No live account, device, search or public personal question. Blank/pass valid. Pre-agree discreet supervised step-out and supported return. Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Do not probe or promise secrecy.
Where this leads
This helps me question information, respect privacy and ask for support in learning, relationships and future work.
